## Summary

Elijas, son of Mošė, the Karaim captain of the Trakai guards (wife Rachelė), keeps the vault door; his younger son [Zacharijas](zacharijas.qmd) holds it in 1430; his elder son is [Samuelis](samuelis.qmd).

## Appearance & tells

A tall man with a grey beard and dark, quiet eyes; a warrior, not a priest (Book II ch. 18; Book III ch. 28). He stands at the vault door the way a man stands who does not know he is entitled to sit (Book IV ch. 10). His rare smile "soft as a hand's touch". Tells: his wife Rachelė's small lamp on a shelf, which the Karaims keep burning in every house; the copper lamp with a three-part wick he brought from Crimea, which his son Zacharijas keeps burning day and night when the hearths of Trakai die (Book V ch. 4).

## Want · Need · Lie · Truth

| | |
|---|---|
| **Want** (external) | To settle his thirty families safely on Duke Vytautas's land and keep their faith. |
| **Need** (internal) | To understand that a door can guard something even when it guards nothing. |
| **Lie** they believe | That a soldier need not explain what he sees on the road. |
| **Truth** they learn (or refuse) | That an empty door, held faithfully, is heavy: he never thought empty doors could be so heavy (Book III ch. 28). |

## Arc by book

- **Book II (1397-98):** arrives at Trakai with thirty Karaim families, sees the dust-pillar of the steppe-spirit crumble at the first pine wood ("We are no longer his"); the Franciscan offers to baptise his children and is turned away with bread; the Grand Duchess Ona visits (ch. 18); in 1399 he lets Vytautas pass with the Vorskla cloak and asks nothing (ch. 29).
- **Book III (1410-11):** stays behind at the empty vault when the lantern goes to Grunwald ("Someone has to stand at a door with nothing behind it, so that someone can come back", ch. 15); the lantern returns after eleven months (ch. 28).
- **Book IV (1418-1430):** at the dinner with the new bride Julijona (ch. 10); his younger son commands Vytautas's escort at the fall (ch. 25), and receives Jogaila (ch. 26); he himself is long in the Karaim cemetery by 1430 (ch. 29).
- **Book V:** his sons Samuelis and Zacharijas; the copper lamp (ch. 4).

## Power & magic

None; a mundane warrior. His own faith keeps a lamp, and the saga goes no further than that parallel (see the Book II outline). He is the witness of the vault, not its keeper: the Karaims are the Steppe-Hunger's refugees, never its servants. He keeps the [flame promise](../magic/flame_promise.qmd) by silence: the graph lists him as keeper of the Last Flame promise at the vault door (1398-1411).

## Record vs saga

- **[Record]:** The Karaims settled at Trakai in 1397-98 (tradition; numbers disputed).
- **[Saga invention]:** Elijas himself and his role at the vault door (Book II ch. 18, 29; Book III ch. 15, 28).

## Pronunciation

Not in the JSON lexicon; derived from the Lithuanian spelling: **e-LI-jas** (/ɛˈlʲɪjɐs/), English sound-alike *eh-LIH-yahs*. The Karaim original *Eliyah* is *eh-lee-YAH*. His father's name is *Mošė* (MO-šė, "Moses").

## Appearances

**Book II:** ch. 18 (Trakų Naujakuriai), 29 and the afterword. **Book III:** ch. 15, 21 (a mention in a letter), 28. **Book IV:** ch. 10, 25 (his younger son), 26, 29, 30. **Book V:** ch. 4 (Užgesusios Krosnys). Continuity: Book V ch. 4 says the Karaims came "from Crimea 33 years before Vytautas's death" (1397); the record's tradition says 1397-98 and disputes the number of families (Book II afterword: about 300, Elijas's thirty being one band).
